sections.title: Family, friends, and possessives
body: Use Det här är … to introduce a person.
Swedish uses han and hon for people, den and det mainly for things; ask rather than assume pronouns.
You may talk about friends or fictional people instead of family.

examples.fi: Det här är min vän Ella.

examples.en: Do you also live in Vaasa?

examples.fi: Ja. Min syster bor också här.
examples.en: Yes. My sister also lives here.

sections.title: Min, mitt, and mina
body: Use min before a singular en-word: min vän. Use mitt before a singular ett-word: mitt barn.
Use mina before all plural nouns: mina vänner, mina barn.
Learn en/ett with each noun because it controls possessives and later adjective forms.

assignment.title: Episode 6 mission: Family, friends, and possessives
assignment.instructions:
LISTEN: Hear the audio twice and answer: Which possessive forms are heard?

READ: Read once for purpose and once for detail. Answer: Who is Samir?

SPEAK: Introduce two people using min/mitt/mina. Try once without the model, then repeat more clearly.

WRITE: Write three sentences about fictional people. Check word order and spelling.

TRANSFER: Change one person to two people.

RETURN: Choose min/mitt/mina for vän, barn, vänner.
assignment.model:
Speaking: Det här är min vän Sara. Hon bor i Åbo. Mina vänner talar svenska.
Writing: Min vän heter Sam. Hans syster heter Liv. De bor i Vasa.
